That places the extension's own computed term at roughly early-to-mid April 2026. The City of La Grange's official ordinance index (lagrangeky.gov/ordinances, checked 2026-07-31 and current through ordinances dated late June 2026) lists 2026 ordinances 01, 02, 05, 07, and 09 through 13 -- covering code-enforcement duties, a zoning map amendment, sign regulations, an annexation, and FY2026-27 budgets -- with no ordinance addressing data centers, a further moratorium extension, or permanent data-center zoning regulations. No City Council action on data centers has been identified since Ordinance 17-2025.
current_status.reason: Direct check of the city's own current ordinance index shows no data-center item among all 2026 ordinances captured on the page, and the November 2025 news coverage establishes the extension's own term already expired months before this pass without further action.

evidence.title: Council extends data center moratorium by 150 days
evidence.supports: Confirms the City Council unanimously approved a 150-day extension after the initial moratorium (approved in June 2025) expired October 30, 2025; the Planning and Development Director stated the earliest the city could act on permanent regulations was its February 2026 meeting, at which point the 150-day extension would still be in place.
evidence.quote: The La Grange City Council unanimously approved an 150-day extension on their data center moratorium, effectively continuing the pause on all data center development within the city limits due to a stall in the enactment of data center regulations. The city's initial moratorium -- approved in June and expired as of Oct. 30, according to the ordinance -- was intended to allow time for regulations on data centers to be drafted and enacted.

decisions.notes: La Grange and Oldham County appear to share a single Planning & Zoning Commission process feeding recommendations to both the city council and the fiscal court (see the companion ky-oldham-county-fiscal-court-2025 decision in this pass). That joint process only reached a second reading of permanent zoning text amendments (KOC 26-920-5) on 2026-07-21 at the county level -- months after La Grange's own 150-day extension would have run out. This suggests a genuine several-month regulatory gap in La Grange specifically, though it is also possible the city took some informal or unrecorded step to keep the pause in place that this pass could not locate. Recommend a follow-up pass to obtain the signed Ordinance 17-2025 text (try requesting it from the city clerk directly, since the CDN link is blocked to automated tools) and to check whether La Grange intends to adopt whatever text amendment Oldham County finalizes.

current_status.to: Still in effect as of 2026-07-31. The Oldham County Planning & Zoning Commission voted unanimously on 2026-06-23 to forward revised zoning text amendments to the Fiscal Court. The Fiscal Court held a first reading of the resulting ordinance (KOC 26-920-5, 'zoning text amendments of the comprehensive zoning ordinance') at a special meeting on 2026-06-29, per the Court's own posted agenda. A closed session on pending/proposed litigation was held 2026-07-14 (subject not specified on the public agenda). A second reading of KOC 26-920-5 was calendared for the Fiscal Court's 2026-07-21 meeting per the Court's own posted agenda. As of this research date, no signed minutes confirming the outcome of that July 21 second reading had been posted publicly, so whether KOC 26-920-5 has been finally adopted -- which would likely supersede the moratorium -- remains unconfirmed.
current_status.reason: Direct review of the Fiscal Court's own posted meeting agendas (a primary source) shows the underlying permanent-ordinance process advancing to second reading 10 days before this research date, considerably more current than the March 2026 news reporting the prior pass relied on.

outcome.from: Proposed permanent regulations were remanded for more work in January 2026; the moratorium remained in effect during revisions
outcome.to: After the January 2026 remand, the Planning & Zoning Commission's revised regulations reached the Fiscal Court as KOC 26-920-5, with first reading 2026-06-29 and second reading calendared 2026-07-21. Passage of second reading was not confirmed in public records as of 2026-07-31; the moratorium (KOC 25-910-508, extended by KOC 25-910-520 'until data center regulations are approved') remains the best-supported operative instrument pending that confirmation.

decisions.notes: The 'extended' classification remains the best-supported status as of 2026-07-31: the Fiscal Court's own posted agendas show the permanent zoning-text-amendment process (KOC 26-920-5) reaching only first reading (2026-06-29) and second reading (calendared 2026-07-21), with no signed minutes yet posted confirming passage. This is a fast-moving situation close to resolution -- if KOC 26-920-5 passed on second reading, the moratorium would likely become 'replaced' within days of this research date. The July 14, 2026 closed session on 'proposed or pending litigation' is also worth flagging for a follow-up pass, since data-center land-use ordinances have drawn litigation elsewhere in Kentucky (e.g., a developer's suit against Simpson County's ordinance). Recommend checking the Fiscal Court's August 2026 agenda/signed minutes for confirmation of KOC 26-920-5's fate.
